title: Поиски загранпаспорта  (Searching for the Travel Passport)

segments.t: In the office, Vika and Kristina pressure Chef Barinov to accept the masterclass because the restaurant desperately needs the publicity during Barani's two-day trip to Russia. Back at the apartment, Max panics when he realizes he cannot find his travel passport before the flight to Cyprus.
Это всех касается.
Между прочим.
А вот зачем, Виктор Петрович.
Он всего лишь два дня в России.
Нам нужен пиар, Витя.
Вот почему я так не хотел туда идти.
Так чувствовал.
Пардон, не смотрю.
А чего вы не на работе?
Мы во вторую смену.
Слушай, Костян, ты не видел мой загранпаспорт?
Просто Кристина предложила Сашу две путевки на Кипр.
А если я паспорт не найду.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Это всех касается.
'This applies to everyone.' Barinov puts that reply around Kostya: the "-sya" ending on "kasayetsya" ("concerns, applies to") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
Между прочим.
'By the way.' Vika jumps in warmly without holding back, shifting the whole mood of the room in a single beat.
А вот зачем, Виктор Петрович.
'And here is why, Viktor Petrovich.' Kostya lays out this answer with warmth: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
Он всего лишь два дня в России.
'He is in Russia for only two days.' Barinov aims this line before Vika: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
Нам нужен пиар, Витя.
'We need the publicity, Vitya.' Vika counters steadily with a nod, to clear the air between them once and for all.
Вот почему я так не хотел туда идти.
'That is why I did not want to go there.' Kostya favors one concrete piece right here: "khotel" means "wanted" (from "khotet"), giving the line its exact edge.
Так чувствовал.
'I had a feeling about it.' Barinov phrases this update before Kostya: spoken Russian trims this down to just 2 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
Пардон, не смотрю.
'Pardon me, I am not looking.' Vika replies boldly around Kostya, leaving no doubt about where she stands.
А чего вы не на работе?
'Why are you guys not at work?' Kostya stresses one vivid piece in earnest: "rabote" means "work" (from "rabota"), giving the line its exact edge.
Мы во вторую смену.
'We are on the second shift.' Barinov gives the remark in earnest: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
Слушай, Костян, ты не видел мой загранпаспорт?
'Listen, Kostyan, have you seen my travel passport?' Vika questions point-blank as Barinov tries to explain the situation.
Просто Кристина предложила Сашу две путевки на Кипр.
'Kristina just offered Sasha two vouchers to Cyprus.' Kostya points to one direct expression with Vika: "predlozhila" means "to offer, to suggest" (from "predlozhit"), giving the line its exact edge.
А если я паспорт не найду.
'And what if I do not find the passport.' Barinov answers boldly with a shrug, to clear the air between them once and for all.
Это всех касается.
Между прочим.
А вот зачем, Виктор Петрович.
Он всего лишь два дня в России.
Нам нужен пиар, Витя.
Вот почему я так не хотел туда идти.
Так чувствовал.
Пардон, не смотрю.
А чего вы не на работе?
Мы во вторую смену.
Слушай, Костян, ты не видел мой загранпаспорт?
Просто Кристина предложила Сашу две путевки на Кипр.
А если я паспорт не найду.

That wraps up this scene as vika and Kristina insist that Claude Monet needs the PR from Barani's two-day visit to Russia, while Max frantically searches his apartment with Kostya for his foreign passport. See you next time!
До свидания!
